progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C01 (Brønsted-Lowry: an acid donates a proton, a base accepts one; ammonia and carbonates are proton acceptors; HCl(g) is hydrogen chloride). Year 11: ionic formulas from charges; polyatomic ion names and charges (sulfate, sulfite, nitrate, nitrite, phosphate, carbonate, hydrogen carbonate, hydroxide, ammonium); balancing; state symbols; acid reactions and the metal activity series (Module 3); oxidation as electron loss (Module 3).
progression.startsWith: Name common inorganic acids and bases. The video opens: Add hydrochloric acid to three different things. A strip of magnesium fizzes. A few marble chips fizz too. And sodium hydroxide solution doesn't fizz at all, it just gets warm.
progression.stopsAfter: naming binary acids, oxoacids, hydroxide bases, ammonia and carbonates from formulas and back; stating the common properties of acids and bases; predicting the salt and other products for an acid with a hydroxide, ammonia, a carbonate or hydrogen carbonate, and a reactive metal, and explaining why each product forms; writing the salt formula from charges and balancing, including two- and three-proton acids; predicting no reaction for a metal below hydrogen; naming the gas test that tells CO₂ from H₂. No indicators, no strength, no net ionic neutralisation, no enthalpy.
progression.nextLesson: the heat given out in neutralisation and how to calculate it (route chem-m6-c03).

teaching.task: Given an acid and the substance it reacts with, how do you name everything, predict the products, and write the balanced equation?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) one acid, three partners, three outcomes (1); (2) the common inorganic acids fall into two groups; binary acids: hydro- ... -ic (2); (3) oxoacids from the ion: -ate to -ic, -ite to -ous, never hydro- (3); (4) bases: hydroxides named as ionic compounds, ammonia, carbonates (4); (5) family properties, caused by acids giving away protons and bases taking them, with strength deferred (5); (6) every acid reaction here makes a salt: positive ion from the partner, negative ion from the acid; formula from charges (6); (7) hydroxide: each OH⁻ accepts a proton and becomes water (7); (8) ammonia: the proton makes NH₄⁺, no OH⁻, so no water (8); (9) carbonate: accepts two protons, carbonic acid breaks into water and CO₂ (9); (10) reactive metal: electron transfer, not proton transfer, gives H₂ (10); (11) only metals above hydrogen; H₂ not H (11); (12) telling the two gases apart (12); memory aid (13); two attempts and brief feedback (14 to 17); decision rule and handoff (18); key notes (19).
teaching.conversationalApproach: one acid meets three partners and gives three results; the video names everything first (binary acids, oxoacids from their ion, bases), then explains each reaction pattern by what happens to the acid's proton (or, for a metal, the electrons), builds each salt from charges before balancing, and closes the hook's three cases one by one. Two exam questions follow with brief feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: Same acid, three different results: magnesium fizzes, marble fizzes, sodium hydroxide just gets warm. By the end you'll be able to name every substance, predict the products of each reaction and balance the equations.
teaching.understandingCheck: (A1) write a balanced equation with states for dilute nitric acid and solid calcium carbonate. Answer: CaCO₃(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) → Ca(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). Crossed mistake: leaving out CO₂. (A2) zinc granules and copper turnings in separate samples of dilute sulfuric acid, with a supplied activity series: predict the observations and write any equation. Answer: zinc fizzes and dissolves, Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g); copper shows no visible change and has no equation. Crossed mistake: "Cu + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂".
teaching.curriculumScope: Syllabus (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, p52; local catalogue IDs C6-IQ1-01 and C6-IQ1-03): "investigate the correct IUPAC nomenclature and properties of common inorganic acids and bases (ACSCH067)" and "predict the products of acid reactions and write balanced equations to represent: acids and bases; acids and carbonates; acids and metals (ACSCH067)". Indicators are chem-m6-c13 and chem-m6-p01; strength chem-m6-c05; net ionic neutralisation and its heat chem-m6-c03.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer. Colour key: the proton (H⁺) teal token as in C01; positive ions amber; negative ions violet; water pale blue; CO₂ grey-green bubbles; H₂ white bubbles; electrons small yellow dots (scene 10 only). Board layout (constant): top-left the short question in one line; under it the equation strip (one equation at a time); the right two thirds hold the naming card, the salt builder or the particle lens; plates in a column on the far left. Reuse: C13 equation strip, charge tiles and crossed chips; C01 proton token and hop; countdown ring; key notes board; painted plates m5x-strong-acid-mg-v1.png, m6-beaker-v1.png, the baking soda and vinegar clip pair, m6-antacid-tablets-v1.png, m6-lemon-v1.png, m6-vinegar-bottle-v1.png, m6-soap-bar-v1.png, m6-household-cleaner-bottle-v1.png, m5x-ammonia-bottle-v1.png, and the C01 litmus pair. New coded items: naming cards with template blocks, the salt builder with charge tallies, the activity series bar. New painted plates (marble, zinc and copper beakers, limewater pair, splint pop, fertiliser granules) are in the Codex asset brief; no hands.

scenes.teachingReason: Brief feedback (feedback 2 (brief)): the answer, the key reason with the givens underlined, and one crossed classic mistake (owner rule, 16 October).
scenes.narrationCue: Zinc / fizzes / zinc sulfate plus hydrogen / Copper / no visible change
scenes.motionPurpose: On the spoken cues: On "zinc sulfate plus hydrogen" the strip writes: "Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)". On "Copper" "Cu" is underlined with "below H"; `m6-copper-acid-v1.png` appears; chip "Copper: no visible change, no reaction". On "trap" a chip "Cu + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂" fades in and is crossed (caption "below hydrogen: no reaction").

On "zinc sulfate plus hydrogen" the strip writes: "Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)". On "Copper" "Cu" is underlined with "below H"; `m6-copper-acid-v1.png` appears; chip "Copper: no visible change, no reaction". scenes.visualReference: the question card writes, each line lighting on its words: "Name the acid." "Spot the pattern: hydroxide, ammonia, carbonate, metal." "Build the salt from the charges." "Add water, CO₂ or H₂ (ammonia: nothing extra; metal below H: no reaction)." "Balance." On "Next" a chip "Next: the heat of neutralisation" appears with `m6-beaker-v1.png` and a small coded thermometer.
scenes.teachingReason: Decision rule and handoff: So for any acid reaction: name the acid, spot the pattern, build the salt from the charges, add water, carbon dioxide or hydrogen as the pattern says, then balance.
